offence_severity: Life imprisonment to transportation for life or rigorous imprisonment for 10 years
physical_harm: Grievous injuries inflicted with sharp-edged weapons and simple injuries
number_of_offences: Charged with multiple offences, including Section 307 IPC; charge under Section 307 IPC was upheld
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation/planning as the accused had openly declared their intention to kill the appellant
motive: To punish the appellant for instituting four cases against Anil Joshi
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the statement of the complainant and the medical report, which indicated that the accused attacked the victims with sharp-edged weapons, causing grievous injuries, and that the accused had expressed intent to kill the appellant.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, relying on their statements to establish the intent to kill and the use of deadly weapons during the attack.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 10.05.2004; Trial judgment: 28.08.2015; High Court decision: 28.08.2015; Supreme Court decision: April 13, 2017
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Manu Sharma, Ms. Ridhima Mandhar, M. Shoeb Alam, Ms. Fauzia Shakil, Ujjwal Singh, Mojahid Karim Khan; Counsel for the State: Jitendra Mohan Sharma, Sr. Adv., Ajit Sharma, Sandeep Singh, Ms. Shweta Jain Pahlad Singh Sharma
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Charge framed under Section 307 IPC; High Court: Deleted charge under Section 307 IPC; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, High Court order quashed and set aside
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused persons, armed with deadly weapons, attacked the victims in a car, causing grievous injuries, and that the ingredients of Section 307 IPC were made out.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the medical evidence did not support the charge under Section 307 IPC and that the intention to kill was conspicuously missing.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the intention to kill or knowledge that death will be caused is a question of fact to be determined based on the evidence, and that injuries need not be on the fatal part of the body to attract Section 307 IPC.
precedent_relied_upon: Anjani Kumar Chaudhary v. State of Bihar and Another (2014) 12 SCC 286
